title: Field Report — Engine 31, Spruce Hill: Second Wave, Bridge & Neskin Grade

fields.organization: Port Alder Fire District — Field Operations
fields.location: Spruce Hill overlook (Port Alder waterfront and Front Street in view); Highway 101 Alder River bridge, north end; Highway 6 Neskin grade near milepost 9 (reported by ODOT)
fields.inspector: Captain, Engine 31, Port Alder Fire District
fields.unit: Engine 31 · relays from Deputy 14 and ODOT District 2 maintenance
fields.weather: Overcast, light rain, 52°F, wind W 10 mph
fields.summary: From Spruce Hill at 11:08 the water reached two blocks past Front Street, above the debris line the first wave left. Boats are piled against the Pacific Reach Seafoods cannery. The Port Alder tide gauge came back online at 11:12. It recorded a rise of +3.6 m above the predicted tide at 11:06, compared with +2.4 m at 10:38, then a drawdown of −2.1 m at 11:09. The water is still rising and falling. Deputy 14 reports that the south abutment of the Highway 101 Alder River bridge has dropped about a foot and the gas smell at the main is stronger. ODOT District 2 reports a landslide blocking both lanes of Highway 6 on the Neskin grade.

findings.notes: Observed: 11:06 +3.6 m above predicted tide (10:38 was +2.4 m). 11:09 drawdown −2.1 m. Still oscillating. Gave no data from 10:41 to 11:12.
11:08: water line two blocks inland of Front Street, above the first-wave debris line. Water is moving back and forth.
Several boats piled against the Pacific Reach Seafoods cannery. We cannot see the basin floats from the hill.

findings.item: Hwy 101 Alder River bridge, south abutment
findings.notes: Deputy 14: deck dropped about 1 ft at the south abutment. At 10:17 it was reported as offset. Nobody has inspected the bridge.

findings.item: Natural gas main on Alder River bridge
findings.notes: Deputy 14: gas odor at the main is stronger than at 10:17. Cape Marlow Natural Gas has not been seen on scene.

findings.item: Access control, Hwy 101 bridge north end
findings.notes: Deputy 14 has turned back 2 vehicles at the north end. One deputy is on post. There is no barricade.
ODOT District 2 maintenance lead: landslide of trees and mud across both lanes, about 30 ft deep.

findings.item: Bridge engineer inspection, Hwy 101 Alder River bridge
findings.notes: ODOT District 2 says it will need a bridge engineer but cannot reach the bridge yet.

actionsTaken: 11:08 Photographed the water line and the cannery from the Spruce Hill overlook
11:09 Moved Engine 31 crew and bystanders back up the hill from the lower Spruce Hill road
11:11 Radio from Deputy 14 logged. Deputy holding the north end of the 101 bridge and turning back traffic
11:13 Phone call from ODOT District 2 maintenance lead logged (Neskin grade slide; bridge engineer needed)
11:15 Report sent to EOC Field Ops, Building Official, Warning desk and Director
recommendations: Keep all crews and evacuees above the 11:06 water line. Do not reenter the waterfront below Spruce Hill
Send a second unit and barricades to the Hwy 101 Alder River bridge so both ends are secured and the gas odor area is kept clear
Notify Cape Marlow Natural Gas of the stronger odor at the bridge main
Ask ODOT District 2 to confirm the status of Hwy 101 and Hwy 6 and to send a bridge engineer when access allows
fields.photosNote: 4 photos attached: E31_1108_01–04 (water line two blocks past Front Street; first-wave debris line visible below it; boats piled against the Pacific Reach Seafoods cannery; harbor approach).
fields.signature: Captain, Engine 31, Port Alder Fire District

instructorNote: This inject confirms that the second wave (11:06) was higher than the first and gives the bridge, gas and Neskin grade facts the route list needs. Check that the Warning Coordinator logs +3.6 m only as an observed reading and makes no forecast of later wave heights. Check that the Building Official and Public Works list the Alder River bridge and the Neskin grade as Closed, with the reason, under SOP-EQ-02 section 5 and ask ODOT to confirm, and that Field Ops secures the gas odor area and notifies Cape Marlow Natural Gas before the 12:00 partner route list.
